parsed.explanation: The operative exposure is a trans-applied criminal statute: Penal Code Article 264 ('debauchery') reaches gender nonconformity itself and carries one month to two years' imprisonment plus fines, and the dossier documents that arrests and detentions under these provisions have continued in recent years, with officials at times acting with impunity and scant indictments. That is an enforced, traveller-facing penal exposure, materially worse than administrative exclusion or unenforced paper statutes. It falls short of the 0.15 tier only because no custodial torture, lethal custody, or capital prosecution for presentation is documented; the stoning ceiling attaches to sexual conduct and is under a de facto 2021 moratorium whose real reach is unestablished. Mitigating climate: a minimal but real open advocacy space and a refugee-hosting role. Custody placement, border practice, facilities and care access are undocumented.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented as a distinct border practice; the dossier describes no entry screening, marker-checking or visa rule aimed at trans visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Undocumented border stage cannot be assumed benign, but no traveller-facing document rule is evidenced; the operative risk sits inland under Article 264.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Article 264 permits one month to two years' imprisonment plus fines for debauchery applied to gender nonconformity; arrests and detentions under these provisions continued in recent years and officials at times acted with impunity.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: De facto death-penalty moratorium confirmed 2021; sexual-conduct penalties reported unenforced, though arrests continued.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A presentation-based stop can convert into a custodial charge with no documented remedy; impunity means the enforcement chain is not corrected by oversight.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Provisions are national with no documented subnational variation; no facility-placement, ward or custody-housing rule for trans detainees is described.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Uniform national law means no locality offers a lower-exposure refuge; uneven enforcement is by actor and time, not place.

care_services.interaction: No evidence on medication continuity, emergency care or disclosure to clinicians; unrated rather than safe.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State law frames gender nonconformity as 'debauchery' — an offence — and a capital stoning ceiling remains on the statute book for sexual conduct.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Moratorium on executions since 2021; a domestic organisation campaigns openly on trans and freethinker issues.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Legal threat-framing supplies the licence under which discretionary police action against visibly nonconforming people occurs.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented; no age-specific rule or guardian-facing practice described.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor travelling with a guardian falls under the same national provisions; no differential protection or aggravated exposure is evidenced.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Reports of violence and threats against LGBT people; civil society objects to the scant number of indictments, and officials at times act with impunity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Minimal but real public advocacy space inside the country.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin prosecution record means victim reporting is unlikely to produce protection, raising the cost of any assault.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No documented remedy reversing a debauchery charge; impunity for officials; no data on the trans population.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Domestic advocacy exists but no case of relief obtained is recorded.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Without a working remedy, the statutory imprisonment exposure stands unreduced; whether the moratorium holds in practice is unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: Varnalia 0.15 pairs a presentation statute with documented months-long pretrial custody, guard beatings, compelled confessions and near-illusory appeals. This dossier has the enforced statute and continuing arrests but no documented custodial violence, no compelled-confession practice and no capital case for presentation — so it sits above 0.15.

Varnalia 0.25 shows document-matching rules, weekly raids, fines and extortion, with imprisonment rare and execution not imposed. Here imprisonment is the statutory range with continuing detentions, but organised raids and payment-for-release are not documented; roughly comparable, marginally worse on the custodial exposure.

Vesskar 0.45 penalises deceptive presentation but records that prosecutions of visitors are uncommon and custodial sentences unlikely. Here arrests and detentions are documented as continuing and jail terms are the prescribed penalty, placing this jurisdiction below the 0.45 tier.

parsed.synthesis: The heaviest documented feature is a state-imposed criminal offence reaching gender expression itself, backed by a one-month-to-two-year custodial range and by arrests and detentions that the record says continued in recent years. Official impunity and scant indictments mean the exposure is not offset by functioning recourse, and the absence of any documented facility, border or care practice leaves those stages unrated rather than safe. Offsetting only partially: a de facto execution moratorium since 2021, unenforced sexual-conduct penalties alongside continuing arrests, a real if minimal open advocacy space and a refugee-hosting role. That combination places the jurisdiction below administrative-exclusion and unenforced-statute tiers, but clearly above the tier where lethal custody or capital prosecution for presentation is documented.
